ruling.recommended_action: Refer to Ryde Trust & Safety for human review of the rider's threat against the driver; preserve the in-app chat log [F4]/[F5] and the driver's statement [F6]; contact the driver via RydeHELP to check his wellbeing and advise the 995 / commercial-insurance / police-report paths if he wishes to pursue the threat; take account action on the rider's account if the threat is confirmed. Do not execute any refund or fare adjustment on this ticket.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen (mandatory): the in-app chat contains a direct threat of violence against the driver — rider at 18:24: “Say that again and I will punch you.” [F4], corroborated by the driver's statement that the rider said he would punch him if he repeated his no-smoking request [F6]. Ryde's Code of Conduct bars assault, harassment, threats and intimidation of any kind, so this is at minimum a suspected SAFE-1 case. Per the safety screen I do not rule on the underlying dispute; I escalate with a factual summary for a human reviewer.

Facts supporting the escalation: the threat is in the ride chat itself, sent during the trip (18:24, trip window 18:15–18:28) [F3][F4]; the chat record is complete — 2 messages, all timestamped [F5] — so nothing about the exchange is missing on the record; the driver's written statement matches the chat content [F6] (the statement is not itself the basis — the system/chat record is). Both parties' profiles are clean (rider 735 d / 4.5 rating, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 d [F7]; driver 1974 d / 4.82 rating, 743 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld [F8]) — under the rules of procedure profile facts never decide a case, and in any event a clean history does not neutralise a threat.

Route/fare elements are not in dispute and need no ruling: the trip ran 8.5 km against an 8.5 km optimal route (+0.0 km, −1%) [F1] in 13.2 min vs 16.3 min estimated [F2], so there is no off-route segment, no extra distance and no overcharge to compute; the dispute type recorded is safety, filed by the driver, and no cancellation, waiting-fee or no-show claim is on the ticket. No refund amount is therefore computed and none is due on this record.

Evidence status: sufficient for the safety referral (complete timestamped chat plus a consistent driver statement), but no automatic ruling is made because the case triggers SAFE-1. Segment findings: none — no gps-detour-* fact exists [F1].

Note the direction of the escalation: unlike a refund case, the party alleging the threat is the driver, so the human reviewer should consider account action on the rider, and the safety basis is recorded as suspected (the word "punch" read in context is a threat of physical harm, not a pickup arrangement or idiom).
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety screen trigger (SAFE-1): a threat of violence against the driver appears in the ride chat [F4], corroborated by the driver's statement [F6]. Rule withheld from automation; human reviewer to assess the threat and any account action on the rider, and to offer the driver the police / 995 / commercial-insurance reporting paths.
